editorialPolicy.authorship: All workout names, summaries, and guide instructions are original Plainstride editorial content. External sources inform distances, pacing principles, warm-up and cooldown structure, and long-run preparation; their prose is not reproduced.
editorialPolicy.medicalScope: The catalog provides general fitness guidance, not diagnosis or medical treatment. Every workout tells the runner to stop for pain or symptoms that feel unsafe.
editorialPolicy.longDistanceScope: The half-marathon and marathon entries guide an already-prepared runner through the distance. They are not substitutes for a progressive training plan, event support, a safe route, or a practiced hydration and fueling plan.

anchors.label: Very easy
anchors.description: Relaxed walking or jogging with effortless conversation.

anchors.label: Easy
anchors.description: Comfortable, conversational running that feels sustainable.

anchors.label: Steady
anchors.description: Purposeful and controlled; speaking in short sentences is still possible.

anchors.label: Comfortably hard
anchors.description: Focused work that can be held for a limited block without straining.

anchors.label: Fast and controlled
anchors.description: Hard running with sound form and enough control to repeat the effort.

anchors.label: Maximum
anchors.description: All-out effort; not prescribed by this catalog.

workouts.title: Guided 1.5K
workouts.subtitle: A short, focused effort that builds toward a strong final 300 metres.
workouts.guideLine: Find control before speed, hold your form through the middle, then build into the finish.
prerequisites: Be comfortable running continuously for at least 15 minutes.
Complete an easy warm-up before starting this distance effort.
Choose a flat, uninterrupted route or a track.

guideInstructions.objective: Run an evenly controlled 1500 metres and reserve the hardest sustainable effort for the closing segment.
beforeStart: Warm up with easy running, then add a few relaxed accelerations.
Choose an effort you can control for the full distance; this is not an all-out sprint.

segments.instruction: Accelerate smoothly, settle your breathing, and avoid spending the first minute chasing pace.
segments.cue: Quick and calm. Leave room to build.
segments.fallback: If the start already feels strained, ease back immediately and rebuild your rhythm.

segments.instruction: Hold a tall posture, relaxed shoulders, and an even rhythm through the longest section.
segments.cue: Stay tall. Hold the rhythm.
segments.fallback: Shorten your stride slightly rather than forcing the pace.

segments.instruction: Begin a gradual build while keeping your arms compact and your stride underneath you.
segments.cue: Start the build. Smooth first, faster second.
segments.fallback: If form is fading, hold the current effort instead of accelerating.

segments.instruction: Lift your cadence and commit to the line without tightening your face or shoulders.
segments.cue: Two hundred to go. Fast feet, relaxed shoulders.
segments.fallback: Keep the best form you can and carry the effort steadily to the finish.

finish: Keep moving easily for several minutes after the distance ends.
Note whether the opening pace left enough control for the final 300 metres.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.

workouts.title: Guided 3K
workouts.subtitle: Three focused kilometres with a patient start and progressive finish.
workouts.guideLine: Let the first kilometre come to you, lock into the middle, and build only when control is secure.
prerequisites: Be comfortable running continuously for at least 20 minutes.
Complete an easy warm-up before starting a hard 3K effort.

guideInstructions.objective: Complete 3K with even mechanics and a controlled negative progression rather than an aggressive start.
beforeStart: Warm up until easy running feels fluid.
Decide whether today is a steady benchmark or a harder time trial and keep the opening effort consistent with that choice.

segments.instruction: Settle into efficient steps and let other runners or early pace changes go.
segments.cue: Settle first. The work comes later.
segments.fallback: Back off until breathing and form feel coordinated.

segments.instruction: Keep your gaze forward, arms quiet, and pace even through the central kilometre and a half.
segments.cue: One rhythm. Relax into the work.
segments.fallback: Reduce pace slightly and protect form if the effort spikes early.

segments.instruction: Increase pressure gradually without reaching for a longer stride.
segments.cue: One kilometre left. Build with cadence.
segments.fallback: Hold the current rhythm if a build would compromise form.

segments.instruction: Commit to the final 400 metres and keep your shoulders loose as cadence rises.
segments.cue: Four hundred to go. Commit and stay relaxed.
segments.fallback: Run strongly to the line at the best sustainable effort available today.

finish: Jog or walk easily until breathing settles.
Record whether the second half felt as controlled as the first.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.

workouts.title: Guided 5K
workouts.subtitle: A steady 5K with patient pacing and distance-based focus cues.
workouts.guideLine: Settle in early, stay smooth through the middle, and finish with control.
prerequisites: Be ready to cover 5K continuously or with planned walk breaks.
Use a safe route and choose an effort appropriate for today's conditions.

guideInstructions.objective: Cover 5K at a sustainable effort, using the final kilometre to finish stronger only when the first four remain controlled.
beforeStart: Decide whether this is an easy completion run, a steady benchmark, or a race effort.
Begin more conservatively than your first impulse.

segments.instruction: Use the first kilometre to settle breathing, cadence, and posture.
segments.cue: Patient first kilometre. Find your rhythm.
segments.fallback: Slow down or add a brief walk break before effort becomes strained.

segments.instruction: Hold the effort you chose, scan for relaxed shoulders, and avoid unnecessary surges.
segments.cue: Smooth through the middle. One steady gear.
segments.fallback: Choose a pace you could maintain for another kilometre beyond the finish.

segments.instruction: If you still feel composed, gradually increase pressure; otherwise keep the same steady effort.
segments.cue: One and a half to go. Build only if you own the pace.
segments.fallback: Maintain rather than accelerate if breathing or form is deteriorating.

segments.instruction: Lift cadence, keep your face and hands relaxed, and run through the distance target.
segments.cue: Five hundred left. Strong form to the line.
segments.fallback: Hold a proud, steady finish without sprinting.

finish: Walk or jog easily for a few minutes.
Save one note about pacing: too quick, even, or room to build.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.

workouts.title: Guided 10K
workouts.subtitle: Patient pacing and progressive focus across ten kilometres.
workouts.guideLine: Keep the first half patient and let your rhythm carry you home.
prerequisites: Be prepared to cover 10K continuously or with planned walk breaks.
Choose a safe route and account for heat, hills, and available water.

guideInstructions.objective: Cover 10K with even effort, avoiding early surges and preserving enough control to run the final two kilometres well.
beforeStart: Pick an effort that matches today's purpose and conditions.
Use familiar hydration if conditions or duration call for it; do not experiment during a goal effort.

segments.instruction: Start below the effort you expect to hold later and let your body warm into the distance.
segments.cue: Two patient kilometres. Save the work for later.
segments.fallback: Ease off or add an early walk break if breathing rises too quickly.

segments.instruction: Hold an economical pace, check posture periodically, and take the route one kilometre at a time.
segments.cue: Cruise the middle. Quiet arms, steady feet.
segments.fallback: Reduce effort until you can speak a short sentence without gasping.

segments.instruction: Stay present as fatigue grows; build gently only if pace and form remain under control.
segments.cue: Three kilometres left. Focus, do not force.
segments.fallback: Hold steady or use a short walk reset rather than letting form unravel.

segments.instruction: Use the final kilometre progressively: first hold form, then lift cadence toward the finish.
segments.cue: One kilometre. Build in control and finish proud.
segments.fallback: Keep the current effort and run evenly through the line.

finish: Walk or jog until your breathing has clearly settled.
Compare the feel of the first two and final two kilometres before judging the result.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.

workouts.title: Guided Half Marathon
workouts.subtitle: A prepared runner's 21.1K guide with patient pacing and familiar fueling.
workouts.guideLine: Break the distance into calm sections, follow your practiced fueling plan, and protect the first half.
prerequisites: Use only after progressive training has prepared you for the distance.
Have a safe route or supported event, emergency contact plan, and appropriate weather conditions.
Carry or locate water and fuel, and use only a strategy already practiced in training.

guideInstructions.objective: Help a prepared runner complete 21.0975K with restrained early effort, even middle kilometres, and a finish based on actual readiness.
beforeStart: Confirm the route, conditions, water access, and practiced fueling plan before starting.
Set an effort ceiling for the first 10K and commit not to chase early pace.

segments.instruction: Let the field or watch go if needed; establish relaxed breathing and an economical stride.
segments.cue: Three patient kilometres. Protect the day.
segments.fallback: Slow down early; small corrections now are cheaper than large corrections later.

segments.instruction: Lock into a repeatable rhythm and follow your practiced hydration and fueling timing.
segments.cue: Settle and fuel as practiced. Nothing new today.
segments.fallback: Walk briefly at an aid point or reduce pace if fueling, heat, or hills raise the effort.

segments.instruction: Run kilometre to kilometre, keep fueling familiar, and make posture the priority when fatigue appears.
segments.cue: Past halfway. Keep the rhythm honest and simple.
segments.fallback: Shift to a planned run-walk pattern before fatigue becomes a crisis.

segments.instruction: Hold effort on hills and into wind; build only if breathing, form, and fueling all remain stable.
segments.cue: Five kilometres left. Focus first, build second.
segments.fallback: Maintain or add short walk breaks; finishing safely is the priority.

segments.instruction: Run the final 1.1K with compact form and increase effort only as the finish becomes certain.
segments.cue: Final 1.1K. Strong, compact, and all the way through.
segments.fallback: Keep moving safely at the best sustainable effort available.

finish: Keep walking after the finish and begin your practiced recovery routine.
Do not make immediate training decisions; review pacing and fueling after recovery.
stopConditions: Stop and use event or emergency support for chest discomfort, faintness, confusion, severe shortness of breath, loss of coordination, or any symptom that feels unsafe.
Stop for sharp or worsening pain rather than trying to finish through it.

workouts.title: Guided Marathon
workouts.subtitle: A prepared runner's 42.2K guide for even pacing, familiar fuel, and safe decisions.
workouts.guideLine: Start slower than excitement suggests, follow the plan you practiced, and make patient decisions deep into the distance.
prerequisites: Use only after a progressive marathon build has prepared you for 42.195K.
Use a supported event or a thoroughly planned safe route with emergency support and reliable location sharing.
Carry or locate water and fuel, and use only hydration, fueling, footwear, and gear already practiced in long runs.
Check weather and event medical guidance before starting.

guideInstructions.objective: Help a prepared runner complete 42.195K through even pacing, practiced fueling, and conservative choices when conditions or symptoms change.
beforeStart: Confirm route support, weather, emergency contacts, location sharing, aid access, and your practiced fuel and hydration plan.
Commit to a conservative first 10K and to adjusting effort for heat, hills, wind, or unexpected symptoms.

segments.instruction: Let excitement pass through without turning it into pace; establish calm breathing and clear space around you.
segments.cue: Five protected kilometres. Easy is the assignment.
segments.fallback: Slow down immediately if the start does not feel restrained.

segments.instruction: Settle into repeatable mechanics and begin the exact fueling and hydration routine practiced in training.
segments.cue: Make it routine. Easy rhythm, familiar fuel.
segments.fallback: Use aid-station walk breaks or reduce pace before small issues compound.

segments.instruction: Take the course in small sections, keep fueling familiar, and resist any urge to race before 30K.
segments.cue: Patient through thirty. Keep stacking calm kilometres.
segments.fallback: Adjust for heat, hills, stomach issues, or rising effort; the original pace is no longer the goal if conditions have changed.

segments.instruction: Focus on posture, compact steps, and the next landmark; hold effort rather than forcing pace.
segments.cue: This is the work. Short horizon, steady form.
segments.fallback: Adopt a deliberate run-walk pattern and use course support before the situation becomes unsafe.

segments.instruction: Keep decisions simple: form, direction, aid, next kilometre. Increase effort only when your condition is stable and the finish is close.
segments.cue: Five kilometres left. Stay safe, stay compact, keep moving forward.
segments.fallback: Walk, stop at aid, or end the attempt if symptoms or conditions make continuing unsafe.

finish: Keep walking through the finish area and accept support if you feel unwell or unsteady.
Begin the recovery routine you prepared, and delay analysis until you are warm, fed, hydrated, and settled.
stopConditions: Stop and use event or emergency support for chest discomfort, faintness, confusion, severe shortness of breath, loss of coordination, or any symptom that feels unsafe.
Stop for sharp or worsening pain rather than trying to finish through it.
Stop when weather, route conditions, loss of supplies, or loss of support makes continuing unsafe.

workouts.title: First Run-Walk
workouts.subtitle: Short running intervals with generous walking recoveries.
workouts.guideLine: Keep every run gentle, use the full walk recovery, and finish feeling that you could do more.

steps.label: Warm-up walk
steps.detail: Walk easily and let your body warm up

prerequisites: Choose a flat, safe route where switching between running and walking is easy.
Keep the run portions gentle; speed is not the goal.

guideInstructions.objective: Introduce running through eight one-minute easy efforts separated by full walking recoveries.
beforeStart: Wear comfortable shoes and choose a route that lets you stop safely.
Plan to repeat this workout on another day rather than making it harder today.

segments.instruction: Walk naturally and let your breathing and joints warm gradually.
segments.cue: Easy walk. No rush to run.
segments.fallback: Continue walking if your body does not feel ready to jog.

segments.instruction: Jog each minute gently, then use the entire ninety-second walk to recover.
segments.cue: Easy run, easier walk. Repeat with control.
segments.fallback: Walk any run interval or end the running portion early; completing every repeat is optional.

segments.instruction: Walk easily until breathing settles and finish without rushing.
segments.cue: You did the work. Walk it down gently.
segments.fallback: Stop in a safe place if walking is uncomfortable.

finish: Finish feeling capable of doing a little more.
Take at least one recovery day before repeating if this was a new effort.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.

workouts.title: Easy 30
workouts.subtitle: Thirty conversational minutes with a gentle start and finish.
workouts.guideLine: Let pace be the outcome, not the target; keep the whole run conversational.

steps.label: Gentle start
steps.detail: Very easy running or brisk walking

prerequisites: No pace target is required; walking is always an acceptable adjustment.

guideInstructions.objective: Accumulate thirty low-stress aerobic minutes while reinforcing relaxed, repeatable running.
beforeStart: Choose a route that makes it easy to keep effort low.
Leave pace alerts off unless they help you slow down.

segments.instruction: Begin slower than your eventual easy rhythm and let your stride loosen naturally.
segments.cue: Start softer than you think you need.
segments.fallback: Walk until your body feels ready to jog.

segments.instruction: Run at a pace that allows full-sentence conversation and relaxed shoulders.
segments.cue: Easy enough to repeat tomorrow.
segments.fallback: Slow down or insert a walk break until conversation feels easy again.

segments.instruction: Reduce pace gradually and finish calmer than the middle of the run.
segments.cue: Ease it down. No finish-line surge.
segments.fallback: Walk the final minutes.

finish: You should finish with energy in reserve.
If the run felt harder than conversational, log that rather than forcing the easy label.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.

workouts.title: Recovery 20
workouts.subtitle: A short reset with permission to jog, walk, or mix both.
workouts.detail: Run or walk · 20 min · very easy
workouts.guideLine: Make recovery the goal: move gently, ignore pace, and finish fresher than you started.

steps.label: Gentle movement
steps.detail: Easy jog, walk, or a mix

prerequisites: Use recovery movement only when gentle activity feels appropriate; rest is a valid alternative.

guideInstructions.objective: Use gentle movement as a readiness check and finish without adding meaningful training stress.
beforeStart: Choose rest instead if walking already feels painful or unusually difficult.
Remove pace and distance expectations.

segments.instruction: Walk and notice whether your body loosens, stays the same, or feels worse.
segments.cue: Check in. Recovery is the whole job.
segments.fallback: End the session if movement increases pain or fatigue.

segments.instruction: Jog only if it feels smoother than walking; switch freely between both.
segments.cue: Gentle enough to feel restorative.
segments.fallback: Walk or stop; there is nothing to complete at the expense of recovery.

segments.instruction: Walk easily and finish as soon as you feel settled.
segments.cue: Bring it down and keep the recovery win.
segments.fallback: Stop early in a safe place.

finish: You should feel the same or better than when you began.
If you feel worse, prioritize rest and reconsider the next hard session.
stopConditions: Stop if movement increases pain, changes your gait, or produces dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.

workouts.title: Speed Run
workouts.subtitle: Four controlled two-minute repeats with complete guidance.
workouts.guideLine: Run each fast repeat with control and use every recovery.
prerequisites: Be comfortable running easily for at least 30 minutes.
Avoid placing this next to another hard workout; allow easy recovery afterward.

guideInstructions.objective: Complete four consistent two-minute fast repeats with enough control that the final repeat matches the first.
beforeStart: Choose a flat, interruption-free route or track.
Fast means controlled hard running, not sprinting.

segments.instruction: Run easily and let cadence rise naturally near the end without forcing pace.
segments.cue: Warm first. Speed comes after eight minutes.
segments.fallback: Extend the easy running or convert the workout to Easy 30 if you do not feel ready.

effort.feel: Fast, repeatable efforts with easy recoveries

segments.instruction: Run each work block at the fastest pace you can repeat evenly; jog or walk every recovery until breathing settles.
segments.cue: Fast and repeatable. Recovery is part of the workout.
segments.fallback: Slow the next repeat, shorten it, or skip it if form or control does not return.

segments.instruction: Reduce effort immediately and keep moving gently until breathing settles.
segments.cue: The fast work is done. Bring everything down.
segments.fallback: Walk the full cooldown.

finish: The fourth fast repeat should look and feel similar to the first.
Follow with easy training or recovery rather than another hard session.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.
End the fast work if your form breaks down or you cannot regain control during recovery.

workouts.title: Tempo 35
workouts.subtitle: A single controlled fifteen-minute tempo between easy running.
workouts.guideLine: Let comfortably hard stay comfortable enough to hold; finish the tempo with the same form you started.

steps.label: Controlled tempo
steps.detail: Comfortably hard; short phrases, never straining

prerequisites: Be comfortable running easily for at least 35 minutes.
Choose a route with few stops so the tempo block can remain even.

guideInstructions.objective: Hold fifteen minutes of comfortably hard running without drifting into a race effort.
beforeStart: Choose effort by feel rather than a pace that ignores terrain or weather.
Tempo should finish controlled, not depleted.

segments.instruction: Warm gradually and wait for the timed transition before increasing effort.
segments.cue: Ten easy minutes. Save the tempo.
segments.fallback: Stay easy for the whole run if you do not feel ready after ten minutes.

segments.instruction: Lift to an effort where short phrases are possible, then hold without surging.
segments.cue: Firm and even. Fifteen minutes, not a time trial.
segments.fallback: Reduce to steady running if breathing becomes ragged or pace keeps fading.

segments.instruction: Drop effort immediately and jog or walk until calm.
segments.cue: Tempo complete. Easy all the way home.
segments.fallback: Walk if easy jogging does not feel restorative.

finish: The tempo should feel like work you could have continued briefly.
Allow easy recovery before the next quality workout.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.
End the tempo block if controlled breathing and sound form cannot be restored by slowing down.

workouts.title: Fartlek Pyramid
workouts.subtitle: One-, two-, and three-minute surges that rise and fall in a playful pyramid.
workouts.guideLine: Change effort, not form; every surge should leave you ready for the next one.
prerequisites: Be comfortable running easily for at least 30 minutes.
Use terrain where changes of effort are safe and do not require sprinting through crossings.

guideInstructions.objective: Practice controlled changes of effort through a symmetrical 1-2-3-2-1 minute pyramid.
beforeStart: Choose effort by feel and terrain rather than chasing identical pace on every surge.
The three-minute surge should be strong but sustainable, not the fastest.

segments.instruction: Warm up gradually and identify safe landmarks for the faster blocks.
segments.cue: Easy first. Read the route ahead.
segments.fallback: Keep the entire workout easy if the route or body does not feel ready.

segments.instruction: Let short surges be quicker and long surges more measured; make every recovery genuinely easy.
segments.cue: Change gears, keep the same relaxed form.
segments.fallback: Reduce the next surge or skip it if the recovery does not restore control.

segments.instruction: Run or walk easily with no final surge.
segments.cue: Pyramid complete. Float it home.
segments.fallback: Walk the cooldown.

finish: The final one-minute surge should feel crisp, not desperate.
Allow easy recovery before another quality session.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.
End the surges if form becomes uncontrolled or the route becomes unsafe.

workouts.title: Hill Six
workouts.subtitle: Six short uphill efforts with full easy recoveries.
workouts.guideLine: Run tall into the hill, recover all the way down, and keep every repeat technically clean.

steps.label: Easy warm-up
steps.detail: Easy running toward a moderate hill

prerequisites: Be comfortable running easily for at least 30 minutes.
Choose a moderate hill with safe footing, good visibility, and a safe recovery route.

guideInstructions.objective: Build strength and technique with six consistent 45-second uphill efforts and complete recoveries.
beforeStart: Inspect the hill and recovery path before the first repeat.
Run by effort; uphill pace is not comparable to flat pace.

segments.instruction: Run easily and confirm that the hill and footing are safe.
segments.cue: Warm up and inspect the hill.
segments.fallback: Choose flat easy running if conditions are unsafe.

segments.instruction: Use compact steps, a slight lean from the ankles, and active arms; walk or jog the recovery safely.
segments.cue: Tall hips, compact feet, full recovery.
segments.fallback: End a repeat early, walk down, or stop the set if footing or form becomes unreliable.

segments.instruction: Move easily away from the hill and let effort fall gradually.
segments.cue: Hill work done. Easy from here.
segments.fallback: Walk the cooldown.

finish: All six repeats should look technically similar.
Allow easy recovery before the next quality workout.
stopConditions: Stop for sharp or increasing pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, confusion, or any symptom that feels unsafe.
Stop the hill set if footing, traffic, visibility, or downhill recovery becomes unsafe.
